equivalents.note: Where the Bengali has kāla the Tibetan song has sgra gcan, 'Rāhu', writing Munidatta's identification of Kāla with Rāhu (cp.01.m2) into the line itself.

Where the Bengali has dhamaṇa the Tibetan song has zla ba, 'moon', taking over Munidatta's gloss (āli, with the purification of the moon), and its commentary (cp.01.m6) then glosses zla ba, not dhavana, as A li.
Where the Bengali has camaṇa the Tibetan song has nyi ma, 'sun', again taking over Munidatta's gloss (kāli, with the purification of the sun), which its commentary (cp.01.m6) applies to nyi ma.

Rendered grub pa here and in grub pa'i slob dpon for siddhācārya (cp.01.m2, cp.01.m6) rather than the glossary's grub thob, and cp.01.m6 once writes ādisiddhācārya as dang po sgrub pa'i slob dpon, with sgrub.

Munidatta's sa eva kālaḥ ('he is Kāla') appears as de nyid kyi dus su, 'at that very time', so the Tibetan reads kāla as time rather than as a name for Rāhu; kālāgni in Kṛṣṇa's verse is likewise dus kyi me.
The Tibetan calls Rāhu tha mal pa'i sems 'dzag pa'i rang bzhin, 'having the nature of the leaking of the ordinary mind', apparently reading cyuti, 'falling', where Shastri's text has acyutirūpo.
A word-for-word calque of mṛgāṅka, 'deer-marked', rather than the ordinary zla ba.

The Tibetan construes bhagavataḥ as the agent of paripakvakuśalāḥ (bcom ldan 'das kyis dge ba rnams yongs su smin pa, 'whose virtues the Blessed One has ripened') rather than with pañcakrama, so the five stages are not called the Blessed One's.
Half transliterated and half translated: paṭa appears as pa Ta ha (as if paṭaha, 'drum') and mañjarī as snye ma, 'cluster', while rāga is rendered glu'i gdangs, 'melody of the song'.
In the Rativajra verse the Tibetan has 'dod pa'i dngos grub, 'the desired accomplishment', where the Sanskrit has siddhir aninditā, 'flawless accomplishment'.
The Tibetan has gzugs la sogs pa'i phung po rnams, without the number five of rūpādayaḥ pañcaskandhāḥ.
Transliterated, and construed with the agentive (ra ti badzra gyis kyang) as if an author were speaking, where the Sanskrit has the locative rativajre, 'in the Rativajra'.
Half transliterated and half translated: saṃpuṭa is kept as saM puT, udbhava is rendered 'byung ba, and tantrarāja is given as rgyud kyi rgyal po.
Here zung 'jug is followed by bcings pa, 'bound' (zung 'jug bcings pa'i ngo bo), apparently rendering naddha a second time; cp.01.m6 has zung du 'jug pa'i ngo bo.

equivalents.wylie: lhan cig skyes pa'i dga' ba

equivalents.note: Where the Sanskrit has the short title Śrī Samāja, the Tibetan gives the full name, dpal gsang ba 'dus pa.
Translated as dpal dgyes pa'i rdo rje (dgyes pa rdo rje in cp.01.m4), not the glossary's kye'i rdo rje'i rgyud.
Both vajra (vajraguru, rdo rje bla ma) and its synonym kuliśa (kuliśāravinda, rdo rje dang chu skyes) are rendered rdo rje in this segment.
By position the Tibetan has khyad par gyis dga' ba, 'joy through distinction', with an instrumental where the Sanskrit has the locative viramānande, and no word meaning 'cessation'.

The verse has sangs rgyas mu stegs, but the prose after it renders buddhatīrthikaḥ as sangs rgyas pa'i mu stegs pa rnams, 'the tīrthikas of the Buddhists', reading the compound as dependent rather than as 'Buddhists and tīrthikas'.
Here rāga is rendered chags pa, not the 'dod chags of cp.01.m4.
The Tibetan reads bdag med pa'i chos, 'the dharma of selflessness', with bdag med pa rather than the goddess name bdag med ma, so this occurrence fits selflessness (nairatmya) better than Nairātmā.
Munidatta's tṛtīyapadam, 'the third verse', appears as rkang pa gsum, 'three verses', without the ordinal pa (contrast rkang pa bzhi pas for caturthapadena in cp.01.m6).
A short form of the glossary's lhan cig skyes pa, in the verse Munidatta quotes.
A calque of śaśin, 'hare-holder' (dkar po ri bong 'dzin pa), in a gloss that the Tibetan heads with zla ba, the word its song has in place of dhamaṇa.
Munidatta's alternative title Dvikalpa is translated brtag pa gnyis pa, kalpa rendered brtag pa, 'examination'.

questions: bhaga (cp.01.m2, cp.01.m4): the term does not occur in these segments; the match is on bhagavat (ভগবতঃ, ভগবতৈব), entered under p-bhagavat.

vajra in cp.01.m4 and cp.01.m6 and siddha in cp.01.m4 match only inside other words (śrīhevajre, vajrasattvasya; siddhir, siddhyanti), so no separate equivalent is given there; the Tibetan has dgyes pa rdo rje, rdo rje sems dpa', dngos grub and 'grub.
camana and dhamana in cp.01.m6 (cavaṇa, dhavana) have no word of their own in the Tibetan, which glosses zla ba and nyi ma instead; see the entries for cp.01.5b.

Not answered because the glossary's Tibetan already matches and the segment uses the same word: bodhicitta (byang chub kyi sems, cp.01.m2, where the Rativajra verse has the short byang chub sems), carya (spyod pa, cp.01.m1, cp.01.m4, cp.01.m5), sahaja (lhan cig skyes pa, cp.01.m2, cp.01.m3), samvrti (kun rdzob, cp.01.m2), p-kanha (nag po spyod pa, cp.01.m2).

Recurring terms are given once, from the verse line where there is one; the other occurrences use the same word, apart from full forms in the commentary (ting nge 'dzin, bde ba chen po), taruvara cited in cp.01.m2 also as lus ljon pa'i shing, and Lūyī named in the commentary as lU yi (pa'i) zhabs for Lūyīpāda.
